You will be met at Campo Grande International Airport and transferred to your accommodation in the Pantanal.

The Pantanal lies in central South America and is one of Brazil's large protected natural areas. Its landscape is shaped by marshy plains, dense flowering vegetation, and clear lakes and rivers. The region is known for its wide variety of birds and other wildlife. Water, open grasslands and patches of woodland alternate, so even a short drive takes you through several different habitats. You will stay in modern lodges where you can relax in comfort after exploring the protected area.

The scale of the Pantanal is clear even on the drive in. Marshes give way to grasslands and winding waterways, and you can hear birds calling, grass rustling and water splashing. The open land stretches far ahead, and the water keeps reshaping its banks. Look for birds, butterflies and other wildlife in the grass and along the water's edge. The region draws nature lovers, photographers, anglers, researchers and travellers who want to spend a few days outdoors away from city life.

Your stay in the Pantanal includes horse riding, boat trips, walks, piranha fishing, birdwatching, photographic safaris and night-time caiman watching.

After checking in at the lodge, you will head out on your first excursion in the afternoon, a boat trip on the Aquidauana River. Centuries-old trees line the banks, and the riverside forest shelters birds, mammals and reptiles. The boat follows quiet stretches of the river, giving you time to look along the banks, listen to birds and watch for movement in the dense vegetation. As evening approaches, the air cools and the water reflects the changing light. The trip ends with sunset on the river.

Overnight at Pousada Aguape.

*The boat trip runs only during the rainy season. If it cannot go ahead, a jeep tour takes its place.*
